cards.title: Culture surrounding 'ideal' childbirth must evolve
cards.body: Letters respond to an article about a five-day labour, with an NHS doctor sharing experiences of feeling 'othered' during childbirth. The discussion highlights need for cultural shifts in how society views different birth experiences.

cards.title: Second baby parenting: what I forgot
cards.body: A parent reflects on the surprises of having a second child, from feeding to teething to digestion. Their mother's practical help has stirred memories of their own carefree childhood.

cards.title: Should AI help with parenting decisions?
cards.body: Tech companies offer eye-movement trackers, personalized podcasts, and optimized nap predictions for parents. The article questions whether parents actually need these tools for managing their children.

cards.title: '18 summers' parenting trend: worth it?
cards.body: Long, unstructured summer days are being replaced with scheduled 'memory-making' exercises. Critics argue this controlling approach undermines the freedom that makes childhood summers valuable.

cards.title: New school rules for AI and devices
cards.body: The 2026 school year brings new device and AI policies, but experts say technology isn't the real issue. The focus should be on what children actually need to thrive in an AI-influenced world.

cards.title: Supporting recovery from eating disorders
cards.body: A new book for families addresses common misconceptions about childhood eating disorders. It offers practical guidance for parents supporting their child's recovery journey.

cards.title: Emergency screening catches teen substance issues
cards.body: Emergency departments successfully screen almost every teen with substance problems, but referral to treatment rarely follows. The data reveals a critical gap in connecting identified youth to help.

cards.title: Gap in children's swimming skills revealed
cards.body: New data shows significant variation in how English schools teach life-saving swimming skills. The findings raise questions about whether children are developing essential water safety competencies.
